title: An algebra is the filtered colimit of the finitely presented algebras mapping to it (Stacks 0BUF)
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $\Lambda$ a commutative $R$-algebra. Let $\mathcal P$ be a set of commutative $R$-algebras, each of finite presentation over $R$ (isomorphic as an $R$-algebra to $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ for some $n,m\ge0$), such that every $R$-algebra of finite presentation is isomorphic as an $R$-algebra to some member of $\mathcal P$ (for example the set of all quotients $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/I$, $n\ge0$, $I$ a finitely generated ideal, together with any further set of $R$-algebras of finite presentation). Let $\mathcal I$ be the category whose objects are the pairs $(A,\alpha)$ with $A\in\mathcal P$ and $\alpha:A	o\Lambda$ a homomorphism of $R$-algebras, and whose morphisms $(A,\alpha)	o(A',\alpha')$ are the homomorphisms of $R$-algebras $\varphi:A	o A'$ with $\alpha'\circ\varphi=\alpha$. Then $\mathcal I$ is a small filtered category (Stacks, Categories, Definition Tag 002V: $\mathcal I$ has at least one object, any two objects map to a common object, and any two parallel morphisms $\sigma,	au:x	o y$ are equalized by some $
u:y	o z$, $
u\sigma=
u	au$), and $(\Lambda,(\alpha)_{(A,\alpha)\in\mathcal I})$ is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the functor $\mathcal I	o$ (commutative $R$-algebras), $(A,\alpha)\mapsto A$, $\varphi\mapsto\varphi$, in the category of commutative $R$-algebras.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0BUF (lemma-ring-colimit-fp-category, line 31771) with its footnote restricting the objects to a set (quotients of $R[x_1,x_2,\dots]$); here the set $\mathcal P$ only has to contain a representative of every isomorphism class of finitely presented $R$-algebras

proof.text: *Step 1 ($\mathcal I$ is small and nonempty).* The objects of $\mathcal I$ are pairs $(A,\alpha)$ with $A$ in the set $\mathcal P$ and $\alpha$ in the set $\mathrm{Hom}_R(A,\Lambda)$, so they form a set, and the morphisms $(A,\alpha)\to(A',\alpha')$ form a subset of the set $\mathrm{Hom}_R(A,A')$; composition and identities are those of $R$-algebra maps (if $\alpha'\varphi=\alpha$ and $\alpha''\psi=\alpha'$ then $\alpha''\psi\varphi=\alpha$). So $\mathcal I$ is a small category. The $R$-algebra $R$ is of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] (it is $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_m)$ with $n=m=0$), so there are $A_0\in\mathcal P$ and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $e:A_0\to R$; with $s:R\to\Lambda$ the structure map, $(A_0,s\circ e)$ is an object of $\mathcal I$. Hence $\mathcal I$ is nonempty (Stacks: '$\mathcal I$ is nonempty as $R\to R$ is an object of it'; here the object is the representative of $R$ in $\mathcal P$).

*Step 2 (two objects map to a common object).* Let $(A,\alpha)$, $(A',\alpha')$ be objects of $\mathcal I$. The tensor product $A\otimes_RA'$ is an $R$-algebra of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-product-finitely-presented-algebras] (Stacks: Lemmas 00F4 and 05G5). The $R$-algebra maps $i:A\to A\otimes_RA'$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$, and $i':A'\to A\otimes_RA'$, $a'\mapsto1\otimes a'$, and the $R$-algebra map $\alpha\otimes\alpha':A\otimes_RA'\to\Lambda$, $a\otimes a'\mapsto\alpha(a)\alpha'(a')$ (well defined since $(a,a')\mapsto\alpha(a)\alpha'(a')$ is $R$-bilinear, and multiplicative and unital because $\Lambda$ is commutative) satisfy $(\alpha\otimes\alpha')\circ i=\alpha$ and $(\alpha\otimes\alpha')\circ i'=\alpha'$. By the hypothesis on $\mathcal P$ there are $C\in\mathcal P$ and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $e:A\otimes_RA'\to C$. Then $(C,(\alpha\otimes\alpha')\circ e^{-1})$ is an object of $\mathcal I$, and $e\circ i:(A,\alpha)\to(C,(\alpha\otimes\alpha')e^{-1})$ and $e\circ i':(A',\alpha')\to(C,(\alpha\otimes\alpha')e^{-1})$ are morphisms of $\mathcal I$, since $(\alpha\otimes\alpha')e^{-1}e\,i=\alpha$ and likewise for $i'$. This is the second condition of Stacks, Categories, Definition 002V.

*Step 3 (parallel morphisms are equalized).* Let $\sigma,	au:(A',\alpha')	o(A'',\alpha'')$ be morphisms of $\mathcal I$. As $A'$ is of finite presentation, there is a surjection $R[x_1,\dots,x_r]	o A'$ of $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; let $y_1,\dots,y_r\in A'$ be the images of the $x_i$, so $A'$ is generated by $y_1,\dots,y_r$ as an $R$-algebra. Let $J\subseteq A''$ be the ideal generated by $\sigma(y_1)-	au(y_1),\dots,\sigma(y_r)-	au(y_r)$, a finitely generated ideal, so $A''/J$ is of finite presentation over $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-quotient-fg-ideal]. Since $\alpha''\sigma=\alpha'=\alpha''	au$, $\alpha''$ vanishes on the generators of $J$, hence on $J$, and factors as $\alpha''= ar\alpha''\circ q$ with $q:A''	o A''/J$ the quotient map and $ ar\alpha'':A''/J	o\Lambda$ an $R$-algebra map. Choose $C\in\mathcal P$ and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $e:A''/J	o C$, and put $
u=e\circ q$. Then $(C, ar\alpha''e^{-1})$ is an object of $\mathcal I$ and $
u:(A'',\alpha'')	o(C, ar\alpha''e^{-1})$ is a morphism ($ ar\alpha''e^{-1}eq=\alpha''$). The $R$-algebra maps $
u\sigma,
u	au:A'	o C$ agree on the generators $y_i$ ($q(\sigma(y_i)-	au(y_i))=0$), hence are equal, as two $R$-algebra maps agreeing on a set of generators agree on the $R$-subalgebra it generates. This is the third condition of Stacks, Categories, Definition 002V; with Steps 1 and 2, $\mathcal I$ is filtered [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

*Step 4 (the colimit $B$ and the canonical map).* Let $D:\mathcal I\to$ (commutative $R$-algebras), $(A,\alpha)\mapsto A$. The family $(\alpha)_{(A,\alpha)\in\mathcal I}$ is a cocone on $D$ with vertex $\Lambda$: for a morphism $\varphi:(A,\alpha)\to(A',\alpha')$ one has $\alpha'\circ D(\varphi)=\alpha'\varphi=\alpha$ by the definition of morphisms of $\mathcal I$. Since $\mathcal I$ is small (Step 1), $D$ has a colimit $(B,(\iota_{(A,\alpha)}))$ in commutative $R$-algebras [lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist], and there is a unique $R$-algebra map $c:B\to\Lambda$ with $c\circ\iota_{(A,\alpha)}=\alpha$ for all objects [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. (Stacks computes $B$ in the category of sets, 'details omitted'; here the colimit is taken in $R$-algebras and only the description of its elements, Step 6, is used.)

*Step 5 ($c$ is surjective).* Let $\lambda\in\Lambda$. The polynomial algebra $R[x]$ is of finite presentation ($n=1$, $m=0$) [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; let $\mathrm{ev}_\lambda:R[x]\to\Lambda$ be the $R$-algebra map $x\mapsto\lambda$, and choose $C\in\mathcal P$ with an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $e:R[x]\to C$. Then $(C,\mathrm{ev}_\lambda e^{-1})$ is an object of $\mathcal I$ and $c(\iota_{(C,\mathrm{ev}_\lambda e^{-1})}(e(x)))=\mathrm{ev}_\lambda(e^{-1}(e(x)))=\lambda$. So $\lambda$ is in the image of $c$.

*Step 6 ($c$ is injective).* Let $b\in B$ with $c(b)=0$. Since $\mathcal I$ is filtered (Steps 1–3) and $(B,(\iota))$ is a colimit of $D$ in commutative $R$-algebras, part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise] gives an object $(A',\alpha')$ and $a'\in A'$ with $b=\iota_{(A',\alpha')}(a')$. Then $\alpha'(a')=c(\iota_{(A',\alpha')}(a'))=c(b)=0$. The principal ideal $(a')\subseteq A'$ is finitely generated, so $A'/(a')$ is of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-quotient-fg-ideal]; $\alpha'$ factors as $\bar\alpha'\circ q$ with $q:A'\to A'/(a')$ the quotient map. Choose $C\in\mathcal P$ with an isomorphism $e:A'/(a')\to C$; then $(C,\bar\alpha'e^{-1})$ is an object of $\mathcal I$ and $e q:(A',\alpha')\to(C,\bar\alpha'e^{-1})$ a morphism. By the cocone property, $b=\iota_{(A',\alpha')}(a')=\iota_{(C,\bar\alpha'e^{-1})}(e(q(a')))=\iota_{(C,\bar\alpha'e^{-1})}(0)=0$. So $\ker c=0$ and the ring map $c$ is injective.

*Step 7 (conclusion).* By Steps 5 and 6, $c:B\to\Lambda$ is a bijective homomorphism of $R$-algebras, so its inverse map is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras and $c$ is an isomorphism with $c\circ\iota_{(A,\alpha)}=\alpha$. Hence $(\Lambda,(\alpha))$ is a colimit of $D$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: for a cocone $(M,(\mu_{(A,\alpha)}))$ let $v:B\to M$ be the unique map with $v\iota_{(A,\alpha)}=\mu_{(A,\alpha)}$; then $w=vc^{-1}$ satisfies $w\alpha=v\iota_{(A,\alpha)}=\mu_{(A,\alpha)}$, and any $w'$ with $w'\alpha=\mu_{(A,\alpha)}$ for all objects has $w'c\,\iota_{(A,\alpha)}=\mu_{(A,\alpha)}$, so $w'c=v$ by uniqueness and $w'=w$. Together with Steps 1–3 ($\mathcal I$ small and filtered) this is the assertion.

Proof written in seven steps from the Stacks proof: small and nonempty (representative of R), two objects under the representative of A⊗_R A' (new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-tensor-product-finitely-presented-algebras for Stacks 00F4(2)+05G5(4)), parallel arrows equalized by A''/(σ(y_i)-τ(y_i)) (Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-quotient-fg-ideal), then the colimit: Stacks computes it in sets with 'details omitted'; here the colimit B is taken in R-algebras (Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-commutative-algebras-colimits-exist), elements of B are represented in some stage (Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-elementwise), and the canonical map B→Λ is shown surjective (R[x]) and injective (A'/(a')) as in Stacks, hence an isomorphism. stmt_deps: added def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra (the statement's inline definition of finite presentation).
